clue.text: Trunk keeping dry in container

indicators.note: the trunk word holds the dry word inside it, as a store keeps its goods

parts.note: the bole is the main stem or trunk of a tree
TT, teetotal, means not drinking alcohol, i.e. dry

explanation.surface: Someone stores a tree trunk in a container to keep it dry.
explanation.definitionFit: A bottle is a vessel for holding liquids, so a kind of container.

clue.text: Fight against work with model

parts.note: OP, short for opus, is a musical work
to pose is to model, as for an artist

explanation.surface: A worker resists a job that involves a model.
explanation.definitionFit: To resist or contest something is to set yourself in opposition to it.

clue.text: Salt shines bad stains

parts.note: a salt is an old sailor, as is a tar

indicators.note: bad suggests the following word goes wrong and its letters end up rearranged

explanation.surface: Salt spills cause ugly marks on shiny surfaces.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Salt' looks like the seasoning but is a sailor, TAR; 'bad' turns SHINES into NISHES.
explanation.definitionFit: Tarnishes as a verb means discolours or sullies, which is what stains does.

clue.text: Strained relations after my previous wife got part of the house

indicators.note: the tension word comes after the former spouse in the build, so it follows it

parts.note: an ex is a former partner, here a previous wife
tension is the state of strained relations between people

explanation.surface: After a divorce, bad feeling lingers over who gets which part of the house.
explanation.definitionFit: An extension is an added room or wing built onto a home.

clue.text: Ship's cargo possibly in!

parts.note: names a sailing vessel that is also a tall drinking glass, the kind of thing a drink is carried in

explanation.surface: A vessel's load, perhaps, is stowed aboard.
explanation.walkthrough: The word is both a two-masted sailing ship and a large glass for sherry or beer, so the 'cargo' may be a drink held in it.
explanation.definitionFit: The word names a fore-and-aft rigged sailing ship and also a large glass, the second holding a drink as a hold holds cargo.

clue.text: Shock therapy that's often applied

parts.note: a shock is a thick mass of hair, and its everyday treatment is a hair wash

explanation.walkthrough: 'Shock therapy' suggests electric treatment, but a shock is a mop of hair, and the routine treatment for it is a hair wash.
explanation.definitionFit: Shampoo is the liquid soap regularly used to wash a head of hair, a shock.

clue.text: Horse, for example, needing plate badly to external appearances

annotationWithheld.clue: Horse, for example, needing plate badly to external appearances

clue.text: All right! A holy animal

parts.note: OK is an exclamation of agreement, meaning all right
pi is slang for pious, i.e. holy

explanation.surface: Someone exclaims approval at a sacred beast.
explanation.definitionFit: The okapi is an African mammal related to the giraffe, so an animal.

clue.text: School leaver to get a lift

indicators.note: to school is to train or shape, so these letters are drilled into a new arrangement

explanation.surface: A pupil leaving school is given a ride.
explanation.walkthrough: 'School leaver' reads as one phrase, but 'School' is the anagram signal working on LEAVER and TO.
explanation.definitionFit: An elevator is the American name for a lift carrying people between floors.

clue.text: Shaping a tree top is a bit of a performance!

indicators.note: shaping a thing gives it a new form, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Pruning the top of a tree turns into quite a production.
explanation.definitionFit: An operetta is a short light opera, a staged musical show.

clue.text: Hooter preceding the Queen's Cup

annotationWithheld.why: Clue held as 'Hooter preceding the Queen's Cup (6)' parses as BEAK + ER = BEAKER, a cup, but the answer held is LEAKER and the crossing HOLLY (6-down) needs L; the grid and clues disagree.

clue.text: Indication given to a head of state for delegate

indicators.note: head of picks out the first letter of the word state

parts.note: a sign is an indication or signal

explanation.surface: A signal is sent to a national leader concerning a delegate.
explanation.definitionFit: To assign a task is to hand it on to someone else, to entrust it.

clue.text: A student following science mostly concerned with the body

indicators.note: the student comes after the trimmed science word
mostly means the science word loses its final letter

parts.note: physics is a branch of science
L is the learner driver plate, standing for a student

explanation.surface: A student taking a science course is mainly interested in anatomy.
explanation.definitionFit: Physical means relating to the body rather than the mind.

clue.text: Nothing to be seen in quiet note

indicators.note: the nothing letter is seen inside the quiet word

parts.note: sh is the call for quiet
O, the round zero, is nothing

explanation.surface: Not a sound can be heard in a soft musical note.
explanation.definitionFit: Soh is the fifth note of the sol-fa scale.

clue.text: Setter's shock remedy for hitting

explanation.surface: A dog's coat is offered as a cure for being struck.
explanation.walkthrough: A setter is a breed of dog and a shock is a mass of hair; 'hitting' is short for hitting the bottle, drinking too much.
explanation.definitionFit: A setter's shock is literally the coat of a dog, and the same phrase is the idiom for a morning drink taken to ease a hangover.

clue.text: Magazine fails and results in potential disasters

parts.note: Time is a famous weekly news magazine
bombs means flops or fails

explanation.surface: A publication flops, causing ruin.
explanation.definitionFit: A device set to explode later is a figure for a looming catastrophe.

clue.text: Two points snapped and got tangled

parts.note: E (east) is one compass point
N (north) is the second compass point
snarled means snapped angrily

explanation.surface: Two tips broke off and became knotted.
explanation.definitionFit: Ensnarled means caught up or entangled.

clue.text: Time during which everybody has an extended… (3,5) 19…copyright that's protective for diamonds

parts.note: all means everybody
an gives the indefinite article A
long means extended

explanation.surface: Everybody gets a longer period for something.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue runs on into 19-down's; only the first part belongs here.
explanation.definitionFit: All along means throughout the whole period.

clue.text: Copyright and failing newspaper's limitations of trade

parts.note: C is the copyright symbol
losing means failing
The Times is a British newspaper

explanation.surface: Copyright problems and falling sales limit a paper's business.
explanation.definitionFit: Closing times are the hours when shops or pubs stop serving, a restriction on trading.

clue.text: . copyright that's protective for diamonds

indicators.note: the that's letters wrap around the copyright letter as a guard

parts.note: i.e. is the abbreviation for that is
C is the copyright symbol

explanation.surface: Copyright protects designs for diamonds.
explanation.walkthrough: This continues 17-down's clue; 'ice' is slang for diamonds.
explanation.definitionFit: Ice is underworld slang for diamonds, from their glassy sparkle.

clue.text: One might follow his advice, of course, and lose

definitions.text: One might follow his advice, of course, and lose

parts.words: One might follow his advice, of course, and lose
parts.note: describes a racing adviser whose picks for a race on a course may still lose

explanation.definitionFit: A tipster gives betting tips on races, which punters follow and may lose money on.

clue.text: Loves top grade diamonds and minerals

parts.note: A is the top grade
D is the card abbreviation for diamonds
ores are minerals mined for metal

explanation.surface: Someone loves fine gems and rocks.
explanation.definitionFit: Adores means worships or loves deeply.

clue.text: Left on the beach, exhausted

explanation.surface: Someone stranded on the shore is worn out.
explanation.definitionFit: Debris carried ashore by waves has been deposited; figuratively, someone finished or spent is in the same state.

clue.text: Old Greek's fortune given to ambassador

parts.note: HE, His Excellency, is an ambassador's title
your lot is your fortune or fate

explanation.surface: An ancient Greek's destiny lies with a diplomat.
explanation.definitionFit: A helot was a serf in ancient Sparta.

clue.text: Information barrier protecting sources of trade unions

indicators.note: the barrier word surrounds the other letters, shielding them

parts.note: a dam is a barrier holding back water

indicators.note: sources of picks the first letters of trade and unions

explanation.surface: Data walls shield the origins of union bodies.
explanation.definitionFit: A datum is a single item of data, a piece of information.

clue.text: Supporter died in the city from drink

parts.note: a bra is a supporting undergarment

indicators.note: the died letter sits inside the city letters

parts.note: NY is New York, the city

explanation.surface: A fan passed away in town after drinking.
explanation.definitionFit: Brandy is a spirit distilled from wine, so a drink.

clue.text: Travel book allowed in vessel

parts.note: go means travel
let means allowed

explanation.surface: A travel guide is permitted aboard a ship.
explanation.definitionFit: A goblet is a stemmed drinking cup.

clue.text: Port in best rum is served in these!

indicators.note: the port letter goes inside the rearranged letters
served suggests something dished up in a new form, so these letters are rearranged

parts.note: port is the left side of a ship, abbreviated L

explanation.surface: Port and fine rum are poured into these glasses.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Port' looks like the wine but is left, L; 'is served' rearranges BEST RUM.
explanation.definitionFit: The clue word refers to the glasses the drinks are served in, which are tumblers.

clue.text: Might one get grime off, leaving a grainy deposit?

definitions.text: Might one get grime off, leaving a grainy deposit?

indicators.note: off suggests letters gone awry and so reordered

explanation.surface: A cleaner wonders if scrubbing grime leaves gritty residue.
explanation.walkthrough: Read as a whole the clue describes the device: the sand runs down and leaves a grainy pile.
explanation.definitionFit: A sand-glass for boiling breakfast eggs leaves a grainy pile of sand when its time runs out.

clue.text: The sort of person who's unhappy to sit out?

parts.note: sad means unhappy

indicators.note: out signals the word sit put out of order

explanation.surface: Someone is sorry to miss the game.
explanation.walkthrough: The joke is that a cruel person would hate to miss out on the action.
explanation.definitionFit: A sadist is someone who enjoys inflicting pain, a type of individual.
